status: Closed — framework-temp lifecycle authority and standalone quickfix recovery are verified
area: Framework close dirty guard / framework-mode temporary claim admission
finding: A change intended to defer shared git-head provenance classified every parseable latest receipt as advisory. A task could therefore close while a foreign task's git-head receipt was dirty. During repair, framework-mode claim correctly rejected ambiguous active task bindings for the same actor, but offered no independent quickfix binding.
expectedBehavior: Only a parseable git-head receipt whose task identity equals the closing task may be advisory. Foreign, malformed, and unowned receipts must remain blocking. Framework-mode must either support a bounded standalone quickfix claim under concurrent same-actor task lanes or fail before mutation with a durable, governed recovery route that does not require binding the change to an unrelated task.
evidenceOrRepro: 2026-08-14: packages/cli/src/commands/tasks/__tests__/scope-lock-diagnostics.test.ts failed with 'foreign latest receipt must remain blocking'; npm run validate:cli failed in the same focused gate. The defect was introduced by b6febba2d changing the predicate from equality with input.taskId to non-null. Restoring equality makes the focused test and validate:cli pass. A scoped framework-mode claim then returned ATM_FRAMEWORK_TEMP_CLAIM_TASK_BINDING_AMBIGUOUS because ATM-GOV-0355 and ATM-GOV-0362 were both active for the same actor.
followUp: No remaining repair follow-up for this finding. The foreign/latest/malformed receipt matrix and framework-mode lifecycle parity cover same-actor lanes, same-lane ambiguity, lane mismatch, expiry, and standalone quickfix binding; broader lifecycle policy review remains separate.
